content:
In a new interview, comedian Kathy Griffin looked back at the hysteria over her notorious photo with President Donald Trump’s fake severed head, calling her public apology the “only mistake” she made during the episode.

Asked what she thought was her “career-defining insult” during a sit-down with comic Ziwe Fumudoh posted Sunday, Griffin said nothing compared to the backlash her gory protest art provoked back in 2017.

“I know it’s hard to believe it now, because it’s been nine freaking years, but it was seismic, it was crazy,” she said. “I had members of Congress calling me at home that day; I had agencies and networks that I didn’t even know calling me to let me know, ‘You’ve ruined your career and your life, just so you know.’”

In the fallout from the photo, the Emmy winner was fired from her longstanding New Year’s Eve gig with CNN and had several stand-up tour dates canceled. Years later, she learned the Department of Justice had seriously considered charging her with conspiracy to assassinate the president.

While Griffin told Ziwe she thinks people can recover from getting “canceled” if they really did something wrong and own up to their mistake, she said that was not her situation.

“I actually didn’t do anything wrong, but I did an apology because I was such a wreck,” she explained. “I mean, they were telling me American service members were going to be beheaded in my name, and they’d be making videos holding up American heads going, ‘This is ’cause of you, Kathy Griffin.’”

According to Griffin, the outcry resulted in some “bad advice from a bad publicist,” who told her, “Make an apology video right now and make sure you’re crying.”

With nearly a decade of hindsight, Griffin told Ziwe, “That was the only mistake I made, was the apology.”

Griffin retracted her tearful apology video just months later, saying, “The whole outrage was B.S. ... Stop acting like my little picture is more important than the actual atrocities the president of the United States is committing.”
